text: What if a four percent infection rate was quietly costing one point seven million dollars a year?
Four percent? That's fine... isn't it?
Let's put a price on it. Cost of Poor Quality, in Lean Six Sigma for Healthcare.
Twelve hundred central lines a year. A four percent infection rate. Forty-eight thousand dollars per infection, from the worked example.
That's forty-eight infections, and two point three million dollars, every year.
Bring the rate down to one percent, and you avoid thirty-six infections, and free up one point seven million.
Split the cost into prevention, appraisal, internal and external failure, and see exactly where the money goes.
